answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments bind each agent's history to a Merkle root while a verifiable delay enforces a time-lock preventing rapid re-registration. The protocol requires staking collateral, imposes slashing penalties exceeding any Sybil gain, and couples a zero-knowledge verifiable delay to guarantee negative expected attack utility under a robust Nash equilibrium. Because the commitment graph forms a marble ridge across a reef of proofs, identity cloning becomes computationally infeasible.
